title: Modules & Tooling
description: How TypeScript resolves modules, what tsconfig options actually do, and how to structure a real project.

challenges.title: ESM vs CommonJS
challenges.whyMatters: You'll hit ESM/CJS interop issues constantly — mixing require() and import in the same codebase is a common source of mysterious runtime errors.
hints: ESM is statically analyzed, CJS is dynamic — this affects tree-shaking and top-level await

choices.label: No runtime difference — TypeScript compiles both to the same thing
ESM is loaded statically at parse time; CJS is evaluated dynamically at runtime
ESM only works in browsers; CJS only in Node
CJS supports top-level await; ESM does not

challenges.title: What does strict: true enable?
challenges.description:
Which of these is NOT enabled by `strict: true` in tsconfig?

  A)  strictNullChecks — undefined is not assignable to string
  B)  noImplicitAny — parameters must have explicit types
  C)  noUnusedLocals — unused variables are errors
  D)  strictFunctionTypes — function parameters are checked contravariantly
challenges.whyMatters: Knowing exactly what strict enables helps you understand why code that worked before suddenly has errors — and which flag to add to tighten up a legacy codebase.
hints: strict is a shorthand for several flags — but not all strictness flags are included

challenges.title: Write a barrel file
challenges.description:
You have three modules in a `lib/` folder:
- `lib/config.ts` — exports `loadConfig`, `ConfigError`
- `lib/http.ts` — exports `fetchWithTimeout`, `HttpError`
- `lib/logger.ts` — exports `log`, `LogLevel`

Write `lib/index.ts` (the barrel file) that re-exports everything from all three modules so consumers can do:

  import { loadConfig, log, fetchWithTimeout } from './lib'

The modules themselves are provided — you only write the barrel.
challenges.whyMatters: Barrel files are the standard way to expose a clean public API from a library or internal module — every production tooling package you'll write or consume uses them.
hints: Or use export * from './config' to re-export everything

challenges.title: Declaration files
challenges.description:
What is the purpose of a `.d.ts` file?

  A)  It contains runtime JavaScript that runs alongside your TypeScript
  B)  It describes the types of a module without containing any implementation
  C)  It replaces tsconfig.json for large projects
  D)  It is required for every TypeScript file you write
challenges.whyMatters: Declaration files are how untyped npm packages get types — and how you add types to legacy JS scripts in your own infrastructure codebase.
hints: The d stands for declaration — no runnable code, only type shapes

choices.label: B)  It describes the types of a module without containing any implementation
D)  It is required for every TypeScript file

challenges.title: Write a declaration file for a JS module
challenges.whyMatters: Writing .d.ts files for internal tooling is a day-one software engineering TypeScript task — legacy scripts get types without being rewritten.
hints: declare module './metrics' { ... } or just declare the functions directly
